  3158                                  ;	I_am	YRTAB,8,<200,166,200,165,200,165,200,165>   ; [SYSTEM]
  3159                                  ;	I_am	MONTAB,12,<31,28,31,30,31,30,31,31,30,31,30,31> ; [SYSTEM]
  3160                                  
  3161                                  ; DOSTAB.ASM (MSDOS 6.0, 1991)
  3162                                  ; YRTAB & MONTAB moved from TABLE segment in ms_table.asm
  3163                                  ;
  3164                                  ;	I_am    YRTAB,8,<200,166,200,165,200,165,200,165>   
  3165                                  ;	I_am    MONTAB,12,<31,28,31,30,31,30,31,31,30,31,30,31> 
  3166                                  
  3167                                  ; This is the error code mapping table for INT 21 errors. This table defines
  3168                                  ; those error codes which are "allowed" for each system call. If the error
  3169                                  ; code ABOUT to be returned is not "allowed" for the call, the correct action
  3170                                  ; is to return the "real" error via Extended error, and one of the allowed
  3171                                  ; errors on the actual call.
  3172                                  ;
  3173                                  ; The table is organized as follows:
  3174                                  ;
  3175                                  ;    Each entry in the table is of variable size, but the first
  3176                                  ;       two bytes are always:
  3177                                  ;
  3178                                  ;       Call#,Cnt of bytes following this byte
  3179                                  ;
  3180                                  ; EXAMPLE:
  3181                                  ;       Call 61 (OPEN)
  3182                                  ;
  3183                                  ;       DB      61,5,12,3,2,4,5
  3184                                  ;
  3185                                  ;       61 is the AH INT 21 call value for OPEN.
  3186                                  ;        5 indicates that there are 5 bytes after this byte (12,3,2,4,5).
  3187                                  ;       Next five bytes are those error codes which are "allowed" on OPEN.
  3188                                  ;       The order of these values is not important EXCEPT FOR THE LAST ONE (in
  3189                                  ;       this case 5).  The last value will be the one returned on the call if
  3190                                  ;       the "real" error is not one of the allowed ones.
  3191                                  ;
  3192                                  ; There are a number of calls (for instance all of the FCB calls) for which
  3193                                  ;   there is NO entry.  This means that NO error codes are returned on this
  3194                                  ;   call, so set up an Extended error and leave the current error code alone.
  3195                                  ;
  3196                                  ; The table is terminated by a call value of 0FFh
  3197                                  
  3198                                  ;PUBLIC I21_MAP_E_TAB
  3199                                  	; 10/08/2018
  3200                                  
  3201                                  ; 29/04/2019
  3202                                  ; DOSCODE:3DE9h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
  3203                                  ; 04/11/2022
  3204                                  ; DOSCODE:3DDBh	(MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)

  3773                                  
  3774                                  ; ==========================================================================
  3775                                  ;
  3776                                  ; $Set_CTRL_C_Trapping
  3777                                  ;
  3778                                  ; Function:
  3779                                  ;	Enable disable ^C checking in dispatcher
  3780                                  ;
  3781                                  ; Inputs:
  3782                                  ;		AL = 0 read ^C status
  3783                                  ;		AL = 1 Set ^C status, DL = 0/1 for ^C off/on
  3784                                  ;		AL = 2 Set ^C status to contents of DL.	Output is old state.
  3785                                  ;		AL = 5 get DOS boot drive
  3786                                  ;		AL = 6 Get version number
  3787                                  ;			RETURNS:
  3788                                  ;				BH = Minor version number
  3789                                  ;				BL = Major version number
  3790                                  ;				DL = DOS internal revision
  3791                                  ;				DH = DOS type flags
  3792                                  ;					Bit 3 	- DOS in ROM
  3793                                  ;					Bit 4 	- DOS in HMA
  3794                                  ;					Bit 0-2, 5-7 - Reserved
  3795                                  ; Outputs:
  3796                                  ;		If AL = 0 then DL = 0/1 for ^C off/on
  3797                                  ;
  3798                                  ; History:
  3799                                  ;      removed	AL = 3 Get CPSW state to DL	    DOS 3.4
  3800                                  ;      removed	AL = 4 Set CPSW state from DL	    DOS 3.4
  3801                                  ; ==========================================================================
  3802                                  
  3803                                  ; 04/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  3804                                  ; DOSCODE:4045h (MSDOS 5.0, MSDOS.SYS)
  3805                                  
  3806                                  ; 01/01/2024 - Retro DOS v4.2 (Modified MSDOS 6.22 MSDOS.SYS)
  3807                                  ; DOSCODE:4052h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
  3808                                  ; DOSCODE:4052h (MSDOS 6.22, MSDOS.SYS)
  3809                                  ; DOSCODE:4123h (PCDOS 7.1, IBMDOS.COM)
  3810                                  
  3811                                  _$SET_CTRL_C_TRAPPING:
  3812                                  	; 01/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
  3813                                  
  3814 00000267 3C06                    	cmp	AL,6			; Is this a valid subfunction?
  3815 00000269 7603                    	jbe	short scct_1		; If yes continue processing
  3816                                  
  3817 0000026B B0FF                    	mov	AL,0FFh			; Else set AL to -1 and
  3818 0000026D CF                      	iret
  3819                                  scct_1:
  3820 0000026E 1E                      	push	DS
  3821                                  
  3822                                  	;getdseg <DS>			; DS -> DosData, ASSUME DS:DosSeg
  3823 0000026F 2E8E1E[0700]            	mov	ds,[cs:DosDSeg]
  3824                                  	
  3825 00000274 50                      	push	AX			; DL only register that can change
  3826 00000275 56                      	push	SI
  3827                                  
  3828 00000276 BE[3703]                	mov	SI,CNTCFLAG		; DS:SI --> Ctrl C Status byte
  3829 00000279 30E4                    	xor	AH,AH			; Clear high byte of AX

  5972                                  ;M044; Start of changes
  5973                                  ; Winoldap has a bug in that its calculations for the Windows memory image
  5974                                  ; to save is off by 1 para. This para can happen to be a Windows arena if the
  5975                                  ; DOS top of memory happens to be at an odd boundary (as is the case when
  5976                                  ; UMBs are present). This is because Windows builds its arenas only at even
  5977                                  ; para boundaries. This arena now gets trashed when Windows is swapped back
  5978                                  ; in leading to a crash. Winoldap issues callouts when it swaps Windows out
  5979                                  ; and back in. We sit on these callouts. On the Windows swapout, we save the
  5980                                  ; last para of the Windows memory block and then restore this para on the
  5981                                  ; Windows swapin callout. 
  5982                                  
  5983                                  getwinlast:
  5984                                  	; 07/12/2022
  5985 00000904 8B36[3003]              	mov	si,[CurrentPDB]
  5986 00000908 4E                      	dec	si

  5989 00000910 C3                      	retn
  5990                                  
  5991                                  ; 15/12/2022
  5992                                  %if 0
  5993                                  winold_swap:
  5994                                  	push	ds
  5995                                  	push	es
  5996                                  	push	si
  5997                                  	push	di
  5998                                  	push	cx

  6000                                  	;getdseg <ds>			;ds = DOSDATA

  6002                                  
  6003                                  	cmp	al,1			;swap Windows out call
  6004                                  	jne	short swapin		;no, check if Swap in call
  6005                                  	call	getwinlast
  6006                                  	push	ds
  6007                                  	pop	es
  6008                                  	mov	ds,si			;ds = memory arena of Windows
  6009                                  	xor	si,si
  6010                                  	mov	di,WinoldPatch1
  6011                                  	mov	cx,8
  6012                                  	cld
  6013                                  	push	cx
  6014                                  	rep	movsb			;save first 8 bytes
  6015                                  	pop	cx
  6016                                  	mov	di,WinoldPatch2
  6017                                  	rep	movsb			;save next 8 bytes

  6019                                  swapin:
  6020                                  	cmp	al,2			;swap Windows in call?
  6021                                  	jne	short winold_done	;no, something else, pass it on
  6022                                  	call	getwinlast
  6023                                  	mov	es,si

  6331                                  ; OEMFunction key is expected to process a single function
  6332                                  ;   key input from a device and dispatch to the proper
  6333                                  ;   routines leaving all registers UNTOUCHED.
  6334                                  ;
  6335                                  ; Inputs:   CS, SS are DOSGROUP
  6336                                  ; Outputs:  None. This function is expected to JMP to onw of
  6337                                  ;           the following labels:
  6338                                  ;
  6339                                  ;           GetCh       - ignore the sequence
  6340                                  ;           TwoEsc      - insert an ESCChar in the buffer
  6341                                  ;           ExitIns     - toggle insert mode
  6342                                  ;           EnterIns    - toggle insert mode
  6343                                  ;           BackSp      - move backwards one space
  6344                                  ;           ReEdit      - reedit the line with a new template
  6345                                  ;           KilNew      - discard the current line and start from scratch
  6346                                  ;           CopyLin     - copy the rest of the template into the line
  6347                                  ;           SkipStr     - read the next character and skip to it in the template
  6348                                  ;           CopyStr     - read next char and copy from template to line until char
  6349                                  ;           SkipOne     - advance position in template one character
  6350                                  ;           CopyOne     - copy next character in template into line
  6351                                  ;           CtrlZ       - place a ^Z into the template
  6352                                  ; Registers that are allowed to be modified by this function are:
  6353                                  ;           AX, CX, BP
  6354                                  
  6355                                  ; 13/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
  6356                                  ; -------------------------------------
  6357                                  ; DOSCODE:4820h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
  6358                                  
  6359                                  ; 05/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  6360                                  ; -------------------------------------
  6361                                  ; DOSCODE:4813h (MSDOS 5.0, MSDOS.SYS)
  6362

  6365 00000A42 B10E                    	MOV     CL,ESCTABLEN ; 14	; length of table for scan
  6366 00000A44 57                      	PUSH    DI                      ; save DI (cannot change it!)
  6367 00000A45 BF[150A]                	MOV     DI,ESCTAB		; offset of second byte table
  6368 00000A48 06                      	push	es
  6369 00000A49 0E                      	push	cs
  6370 00000A4A 07                      	pop	es
  6371 00000A4B F2AE                    	REPNE   SCASB                   ; Look it up in the table
  6372 00000A4D 07                      	pop	es

  6853                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  6854                                  
  6855                                  ; 05/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  6856                                  ; DOSCODE:4A0Fh (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  6857                                  
  6858                                  _$GET_VERSION:
  6859                                  
  6860                                  ; Inputs:
  6861                                  ;       None
  6862                                  ; Function:
  6863                                  ;       Return MS-DOS version number
  6864                                  ; Outputs:
  6865                                  ;       OEM number in BH
  6866                                  ;       User number in BL:CX (24 bits)
  6867                                  ;       Version number as AL.AH in binary
  6868                                  ;       NOTE: On pre 1.28 DOSs AL will be zero
  6869                                  
  6870                                  ; MSDOS 6.0
  6871                                  ;
  6872                                  ;	Fake_Count is used to lie about the version numbers to support
  6873                                  ;	old binarys. See ms_table.asm for more info.
  6874                                  ;
  6875                                  ;		if input al = 00
  6876                                  ;		  (bh) = OEM number			
  6877                                  ;		else if input al = 01
  6878                                  ;		  (bh) = version flags
  6879                                  ;		 
  6880                                  ;		       	 bits 0-2 = DOS internal revision
  6881                                  ;		       	 bits 3-7 = DOS type flags
  6882                                  ;		              bit 3    = DOS is in ROM
  6883                                  ;		              bit 4    = DOS in in HMA
  6884                                  ;		              bits 5-7 = reserved
  6885                                  ;               M007 change - only bit 3 is now valid. Other bits
  6886                                  ;               are 0 when AL = 1
  6887                                  
  6888                                  	; 06/01/2024 (PCDOS 7.1 IBMDOS.COM)

  6898

  6900                                  	;MOV	BX,[USERNUM+2]
  6901                                          ;MOV	CX,[USERNUM]
  6902                                  
  6903                                  	; 13/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
  6904                                  
  6905                                  	;If AL == 1, ROMDOS will return BH = dos internal version # &
  6906                                  	;DOS flags

  6980                                  ;BREAK <$International - return country-dependent information>
  6981                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  6982                                  ;
  6983                                  ; Procedure Name : $INTERNATIONAL
  6984                                  ;
  6985                                  ; Inputs:
  6986                                  ;	MOV	AH,International
  6987                                  ;	MOV	AL,country	(al = 0 => current country)
  6988                                  ;      [MOV	BX,country]
  6989                                  ;	LDS	DX,block
  6990                                  ;	INT	21
  6991                                  ; Function:
  6992                                  ;	give users an idea of what country the application is running
  6993                                  ; Outputs:
  6994                                  ;	IF DX != -1 on input (get country)
  6995                                  ;	  AL = 0 means return current country table.
  6996                                  ;	  0<AL<0FFH means return country table for country AL
  6997                                  ;	  AL = 0FF means return country table for country BX
  6998                                  ;	  No Carry:
  6999                                  ;	     Register BX will contain the 16-bit country code.
  7000                                  ;	     Register AL will contain the low 8 bits of the country code.
  7001                                  ;	     The block pointed to by DS:DX is filled in with the information
  7002                                  ;	     for the particular country.
  7003                                  ;		BYTE  Size of this table excluding this byte and the next
  7004                                  ;		BYTE  Country code represented by this table
  7005                                  ;			A sequence of n bytes, where n is the number specified
  7006                                  ;			by the first byte above and is not > internat_block_max,
  7007                                  ;			in the correct order for being returned by the
  7008                                  ;			INTERNATIONAL call as follows:
  7009                                  ;		WORD	Date format 0=mdy, 1=dmy, 2=ymd
  7010                                  ;		5 BYTE	Currency symbol null terminated
  7011                                  ;		2 BYTE	thousands separator null terminated
  7012                                  ;		2 BYTE	Decimal point null terminated
  7013                                  ;		2 BYTE	Date separator null terminated
  7014                                  ;		2 BYTE	Time separator null terminated

  7870                                  ;**	$Char_Oper - Manipulate Switch Character
  7871                                  ;
  7872                                  ;	This function was put in to facilitate XENIX path/switch compatibility
  7873                                  ;
  7874                                  ;	ENTRY	AL = function:

  7876                                  ;		    1 - set switch char (char in DL)

  8069                                  ;BREAK <$Parse_File_Descriptor -- Parse an arbitrary string into an FCB>
  8070                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  8071                                  ; Inputs:
  8072                                  ;       DS:SI Points to a command line
  8073                                  ;       ES:DI Points to an empty FCB
  8074                                  ;       Bit 0 of AL = 1 At most one leading separator scanned off
  8075                                  ;                   = 0 Parse stops if separator encountered
  8076                                  ;       Bit 1 of AL = 1 If drive field blank in command line - leave FCB
  8077                                  ;                   = 0  "    "    "     "         "      "  - put 0 in FCB
  8078                                  ;       Bit 2 of AL = 1 If filename field blank - leave FCB
  8079                                  ;                   = 0  "       "      "       - put blanks in FCB
  8080                                  ;       Bit 3 of AL = 1 If extension field blank - leave FCB
  8081                                  ;                   = 0  "       "      "        - put blanks in FCB
  8082                                  ; Function:
  8083                                  ;       Parse command line into FCB
  8084                                  ; Returns:
  8085                                  ;       AL = 1 if '*' or '?' in filename or extension, 0 otherwise
  8086                                  ;       DS:SI points to first character after filename
  8087                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  8088                                  
  8089                                  _$PARSE_FILE_DESCRIPTOR:
  8090 00000EFD E8823E                  	call	MAKEFCB
  8091 00000F00 56                      	PUSH    SI
  8092 00000F01 E87DF5                  	call	Get_User_Stack
  8093                                  	;pop	word [si+8]
  8094 00000F04 8F4408                  	POP     word [SI+user_env.user_SI]
  8095 00000F07 C3                      	retn

  8555                                  ;
  8556                                  ;	There has been a bug in our fatsize calculation for so long
  8557                                  ;	  that we can't correct it now without causing some user to
  8558                                  ;	  experience data loss. There are even cases where allowing
  8559                                  ;	  the number of clusters to exceed the fats is the optimal
  8560                                  ;	  case -- where adding 2 more fat sectors would make the
  8561                                  ;	  data field smaller so that there's nothing to use the extra
  8562                                  ;	  fat sectors for.
  8563                                  ;
  8564                                  ;	Note that this bug had very minor known symptoms. CHKDSK would
  8565                                  ;	  still report that there was a cluster left when the disk was
  8566                                  ;	  actually full. Very graceful failure for a corrupt system
  8567                                  ;	  configuration. There may be worse cases that were never
  8568                                  ;	  properly traced back to this bug. The problem cases only
  8569                                  ;	  occurred when partition sizes were very near FAT sector
  8570                                  ;	  rounding boundaries, which were rare cases.
  8571                                  ;
  8572                                  ;	Also, it's possible that some third-party partition program might
  8573                                  ;	  create a partition that had a less-than-perfect FAT calculation
  8574                                  ;	  scheme. In this hypothetical case, the number of allocation
  8575                                  ;	  clusters which don't actually have FAT entries to represent
  8576                                  ;	  them might be larger and might create a more catastrophic
  8577                                  ;	  failure. So we'll provide the safeguard of limiting the
  8578                                  ;	  max_cluster to the amount that will fit in the FATs.
  8579                                  ;
  8580                                  ;	ax = maximum legal cluster, ES:BP -> dpb
  8581                                  
  8582                                  ;	make sure the number of fat sectors is actually enough to
  8583                                  ;	  hold that many clusters. otherwise, back the number of
  8584                                  ;	  clusters down
  8585                                  
  8586                                  	; 15/12/2022
  8587                                  	; bx = number of clusters
  8588                                  
  8589                                  	; 19/07/2018 - Retro DOS v3.0
  8590                                  	; MSDOS 6.0
  8591                                  	; 15/12/2022
  8592                                  	;mov	bx,ax			; remember calculated # clusters

  8594                                  	; 01/08/2018 (MSDOS 3.3)

  8932                                  	; (MSDOS 6.0 note)
  8933                                  	;
  8934                                  	; The address in BX:AX will be F01D:FEF0 if there is 64K or more 
  8935                                  	; memory in the system. This is equivalent to 0:c0 if A20 is OFF.
  8936                                  	; If DOS is in HMA this equivalence is no longer valid as A20 is ON.
  8937                                  	; But the BIOS which now resides in FFFF:30 has 5 bytes in FFFF:D0
  8938                                  	; (F01D:FEF0) which is the same as the ones in 0:C0, thereby 
  8939                                  	; making this equvalence valid for this particular case. If however
  8940                                  	; there is less than 64K remaining the address in BX:AX will not 
  8941                                  	; be the same as above. We will then stuff 0:c0, the call 5 address
  8942                                  	; into the PSP.
  8943                                  	;
  8944                                  	; Therefore for the case where there is less than 64K remaining in 
  8945                                  	; the system old CPM Apps that look at PSP:6 to determine memory
  8946                                  	; requirements will not work. Call 5, however will continue to work
  8947                                  	; for all cases.
  8948                                  	;

  8951                                  	;mov	[8],bx

  9688                                  ;============================================================================
  9689                                  ; CRIT.ASM, MSDOS 6.0, 1991
  9690                                  ;============================================================================
  9691                                  ; 12/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
  9692                                  
  9693                                  ; Critical Section Routines
  9694                                  
  9695                                  ; MSDOS 6.21 - MSDOS.SYS - DOSCODE:513Ah
  9696                                  
  9697                                  ; 06/11/2022 - Retro DOS v4.0 (Modified MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  9698                                  ; DOSCODE:5126h (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS)
  9699                                  
  9700                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  9701                                  ; Each handler must leave everything untouched; including flags!
  9702                                  ;
  9703                                  ; Sleaze for time savings: first instruction is a return. This is patched
  9704                                  ; by the sharer to be a PUSH AX to complete the correct routines.
  9705                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  9706                                  
  9707                                  ; (DOSMAC.INC, MSDOS 6.0, 1991)
  9708                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  9709                                  ; Some old versions of the 80286 have a bug in the chip. The popf instruction
  9710                                  ; will enable interrupts. Therefore in a section of code with interrupts
  9711                                  ; disabled and you need a popf instruction use the 'popff' macro instead.

 10092                                  ; They assume ES and DS NOTHING, while not strictly correct, this forces data
 10093                                  ; references to be SS or CS relative which is desired.

 10096                                  
 10097                                  ;	TITLE	CPMIO2 - device IO for MSDOS
 10098                                  ;	NAME	CPMIO2
 10099                                  
 10100                                  ;
 10101                                  ;	Microsoft Confidential
 10102                                  ;	Copyright (C) Microsoft Corporation 1991
 10103                                  ;	All Rights Reserved.
 10104                                  ;
 10105                                  
 10106                                  ;**	Old style CP/M 1-12 system calls to talk to reserved devices
 10107                                  ;
 10108                                  ;	$Std_Con_Input
 10109                                  ;	$Std_Con_Output
 10110                                  ;	OUTT
 10111                                  ;	TAB
 10112                                  ;	BUFOUT
 10113                                  ;	$Std_Aux_Input
 10114                                  ;	$Std_Aux_Output
 10115                                  ;	$Std_Printer_Output

 10117                                  ;	$Std_Con_Input_Flush
 10118                                  ;
 10119                                  ;	Revision History:
 10120                                  ;
 10121                                  ;	  AN000	 version 4.00 - Jan. 1988
 10122                                  
 10123                                  ; The following routines form the console I/O group (funcs 1,2,6,7,8,9,10,11).
 10124                                  ; They assume ES and DS NOTHING, while not strictly correct, this forces data
 10125                                  ; references to be SS or CS relative which is desired.
 10126                                  
 10127                                  ;DOSCODE SEGMENT
 10128                                  ;	ASSUME	SS:DOSDATA,CS:DOSCODE
 10129                                  
 10130                                  
 10131                                  ;hkn; 	All the variables use SS override or DS. Therefore there is
 10132                                  ;hkn;	no need to specifically set up any seg regs unless SS assumption is
 10133                                  ;hkn;	not valid. 
 10134                                  
 10135                                  ; DOSCODE:51BAh (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
 10136                                  ; 08/11/2022
 10137                                  ; DOSCODE:51A6h (MSDOS 5.0, MSDOS.SYS)
 10138                                  
 10139                                  ;
 10140                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 10141                                  ;
 10142                                  ; Procedure : $Std_Con_Input_No_Echo
 10143                                  ;
 10144                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 10145                                  ;
 10146                                  
 10147                                  _$STD_CON_INPUT_NO_ECHO:   ;System call 8
 10148                                  
 10149                                  ; Inputs:
 10150                                  ;	None
 10151                                  ; Function:
 10152                                  ;	Input character from console, no echo
 10153                                  ; Returns:
 10154                                  ;	AL = character
 10155                                  
 10156 0000134C 1E                      	push	ds
 10157 0000134D 56                      	push	si
 10158                                  INTEST:
 10159 0000134E E8813C                  	call	STATCHK
 10160 00001351 753A                    	jnz	short GET ; 08/09/2018
 10161                                  ;*************************************************************************
 10162                                  ;hkn; SS override
 10163 00001353 36803E[A00A]00          	cmp	byte [SS:PRINTER_FLAG],0  ; is printer idle?
 10164 00001359 7505                    	jnz	short no_sys_wait
 10165 0000135B B405                    	mov	ah,5			; get input status with system wait
 10166 0000135D E8D82F                  	call	IOFUNC
 10167                                  no_sys_wait:
 10168                                  ;**************************************************************************
 10169 00001360 B484                    	MOV	AH,84h
 10170 00001362 CD2A                    	INT	int_IBM	 ; int 2Ah
 10171                                  
 10172                                  ;;; 7/15/86  update the date in the idle loop
 10173                                  ;;; Dec 19, 1986 D.C.L. changed following CMP to Byte Ptr from Word Ptr
 10174                                  ;;;;		 to shorten loop in consideration of the PC Convertible
 10175                                  
 10176                                  ;hkn; SS override
 10177 00001364 36803E[910D]FF          	CMP	byte [SS:DATE_FLAG],-1	; date is updated may be every
 10178 0000136A 751A                    	JNZ	short NoUpdate		; 65535 x ? ms if no one calls
 10179                                  
 10180 0000136C 50                      	PUSH	AX
 10181 0000136D 53                      	PUSH	BX			; following is tricky,
 10182 0000136E 51                      	PUSH	CX			; it may be called by critical handler
 10183 0000136F 52                      	PUSH	DX			; at that time, DEVCALL is used by
 10184                                  					; other's READ or WRITE
 10185 00001370 1E                      	PUSH	DS			; save DS = SFT's segment
 10186                                  
 10187                                  ;hkn; READTIME must use ds = DOSDATA
 10188                                  ;hkn;	PUSH	CS			; READTIME must use DS=CS
 10189                                  
 10190 00001371 16                      	PUSH	SS ; 04/05/2019
 10191 00001372 1F                      	POP	DS
 10192                                  
 10193                                  	;MOV	AX,0			; therefore, we save DEVCALL
 10194                                  	; 26/06/2024
 10195 00001373 31C0                    	xor	ax,ax
 10196 00001375 E89102                  	CALL	Save_Restore_Packet	; save DEVCALL packet
 10197                                  	;invoke	READTIME		; readtime
 10198 00001378 E88FF7                  	call	READTIME
 10199 0000137B B80100                  	MOV	AX,1
 10200 0000137E E88802                  	CALL	Save_Restore_Packet	; restore DEVCALL packet
 10201                                  
 10202                                  ;	; MSDOS 3.3 (IBMDOS.COM, Offset 1F8Ch)
 10203                                  ;	; (MSDOS 6.0 code does not contain IBM DOS FETCHI_TAG check)
 10204                                  ;	push	bx
 10205                                  ;	mov	bx,DATE_FLAG
 10206                                  ;	add	bx,2  ; mov bx,FETCHI_FLAG
 10207                                  ;	cmp	word [cs:bx],5872h
 10208                                  ;	jz	short FETCHI_TAG_chk_ok
 10209                                  ;	call	DOSINIT
 10210                                  ;FETCHI_TAG_chk_ok:
 10211                                  ;	pop	bx
 10212                                  
 10213 00001381 1F                      	POP	DS			; restore DS
 10214 00001382 5A                      	POP	DX
 10215 00001383 59                      	POP	CX
 10216 00001384 5B                      	POP	BX
 10217 00001385 58                      	POP	AX
 10218                                  NoUpdate:
 10219                                  
 10220                                  ;hkn; SS override
 10221 00001386 36FF06[910D]            	INC	word [SS:DATE_FLAG]
 10222                                  
 10223                                  ;;; 7/15/86 ;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
 10224 0000138B EBC1                    	JMP	short INTEST
 10225                                  GET:
 10226 0000138D 30E4                    	XOR	AH,AH
 10227 0000138F E8A62F                  	call	IOFUNC
 10228 00001392 5E                      	POP	SI
 10229 00001393 1F                      	POP	DS
 10230                                  ;;; 7/15/86
 10231                                  
 10232                                  ;hkn; SS override
 10233                                  	; MSDOS 6.0
 10234 00001394 36C606[900D]00          	MOV	BYTE [SS:SCAN_FLAG],0
 10235                                  	;
 10236 0000139A 3C00                    	CMP	AL,0	    ; extended code ( AL )
 10237 0000139C 7505                    	JNZ	short noscan
 10238                                  
 10239                                  ;hkn; SS override
 10240                                  	;MOV	BYTE [SS:SCAN_FLAG],1 ; set this flag for ALT_Q key
 10241                                  	; 20/06/2023
 10242 0000139E 36FE06[900D]            	inc	byte [SS:SCAN_FLAG]
 10243                                  noscan:
 10244 000013A3 C3                      	retn
 10245                                  ;
 10246                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 10247                                  ;
 10248                                  ;**	$STD_CON_STRING_OUTPUT - Console String Output
 10249                                  ;
 10250                                  ;
 10251                                  ;	ENTRY	(DS:DX) Point to output string '$' terminated
 10252                                  ;	EXIT	none
 10253                                  ;	USES	ALL
 10254                                  ;
 10255                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 10256                                  ;
 10257                                  
 10258                                  _$STD_CON_STRING_OUTPUT:	;System call 9
 10259                                  
 10260 000013A4 89D6                    	mov	si,dx
 10261                                  STRING_OUT1:	
 10262 000013A6 AC                      	lodsb
 10263 000013A7 3C24                    	cmp	al,'$'
 10264 000013A9 74F8                    	je	short noscan
 10265                                  NEXT_STR1:
 10266 000013AB E88702                  	call	OUTT
 10267 000013AE EBF6                    	jmp	short STRING_OUT1
 10268                                  
 10269                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 10270                                  ;
 10271                                  ;**	$STD_CON_STRING_INPUT - Input Line from Console
 10272                                  ;

 11598                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 11599                                  ;
 11600                                  ;   $Get_FCB_Position - look at an FCB, retrieve the current position from the
 11601                                  ;	extent and next record field and set the random record field to point
 11602                                  ;	to that record
 11603                                  ;
 11604                                  ;   Inputs:	DS:DX point to a possible extended FCB
 11605                                  ;   Outputs:	The random record field of the FCB is set to the current record

 11940                                  
 11941                                  ;Break <Misbehavior fixers>
 11942                                  ;
 11943                                  ;   FCBs suffer from several problems. First, they are maintained in the
 11944                                  ;   user's space so he may move them at will. Second, they have a small
 11945                                  ;   reserved area that may be used for system information. Third, there was
 11946                                  ;   never any "rules for behavior" for FCBs; there was no protocol for their
 11947                                  ;   usage.
 11948                                  ;
 11949                                  ;   This results in the following misbehavior:
 11950                                  ;
 11951                                  ;	infinite opens of the same file:
 11952                                  ;
 11953                                  ;	While (TRUE) {			While (TRUE) {
 11954                                  ;	    FCBOpen (FCB);		    FCBOpen (FCB);
 11955                                  ;	    Read (FCB); 		    Write (FCB);
 11956                                  ;	    }				    }
 11957                                  ;
 11958                                  ;	infinite opens of different files:
 11959                                  ;
 11960                                  ;	While (TRUE) {			While (TRUE) {
 11961                                  ;	    FCBOpen (FCB[i++]); 	    FCBOpen (FCB[i++]);
 11962                                  ;	    Read (FCB); 		    Write (FCB);
 11963                                  ;	    }				    }
 11964                                  ;
 11965                                  ;	multiple closes of the same file:
 11966                                  ;
 11967                                  ;	FCBOpen (FCB);
 11968                                  ;	while (TRUE)
 11969                                  ;	    FCBClose (FCB);
 11970                                  ;
 11971                                  ;	I/O after closing file:
 11972                                  ;
 11973                                  ;	FCBOpen (FCB);
 11974                                  ;	while (TRUE) {
 11975                                  ;	    FCBWrite (FCB);
 11976                                  ;	    FCBClose (FCB);
 11977                                  ;	    }
 11978                                  ;
 11979                                  ;   The following is am implementation of a methodology for emulating the
 11980                                  ;   above with the exception of I/O after close. We are NOT attempting to
 11981                                  ;   resolve that particular misbehavior. We will enforce correct behaviour in
 11982                                  ;   FCBs when they refer to a network file or when there is file sharing on
 11983                                  ;   the local machine.
 11984                                  ;
 11985                                  ;   The reserved fields of the FCB (10 bytes worth) is divided up into various
 11986                                  ;   structures depending on the file itself and the state of operations of the
 11987                                  ;   OS. The information contained in this reserved field is enough to
 11988                                  ;   regenerate the SFT for the local non-shared file. It is assumed that this
 11989                                  ;   regeneration procedure may be expensive. The SFT for the FCB is
 11990                                  ;   maintained in a LRU cache as the ONLY performance inprovement.
 11991                                  ;
 11992                                  ;   No regeneration of SFTs is attempted for network FCBs.
 11993                                  ;
 11994                                  ;   To regenerate the SFT for a local FCB, it is necessary to determine if the
 11995                                  ;   file sharer is working. If the file sharer is present then the SFT is not
 11996                                  ;   regenerated.
 11997                                  ;
 11998                                  ;   Finally, if there is no local sharing, the full name of the file is no
 11999                                  ;   longer available. We can make up for this by using the following
 12000                                  ;   information:
 12001                                  ;
 12002                                  ;	The Drive number (from the DPB).
 12003                                  ;	The physical sector of the directory that contains the entry.
 12004                                  ;	The relative position of the entry in the sector.
 12005                                  ;	The first cluster field.
 12006                                  ;	The last used SFT.
 12007                                  ;      OR In the case of a device FCB
 12008                                  ;	The low 6 bits of sf_flags (indicating device type)
 12009                                  ;	The pointer to the device header
 12010                                  ;
 12011                                  ;   We read in the particular directory sector and examine the indicated
 12012                                  ;   directory entry. If it matches, then we are kosher; otherwise, we fail.
 12013                                  ;
 12014                                  ;   Some key items need to be remembered:
 12015                                  ;
 12016                                  ;	Even though we are caching SFTs, they may contain useful sharing
 12017                                  ;	information. We enforce good behavior on the FCBs.
 12018                                  ;
 12019                                  ;	Network support must not treat FCBs as impacting the ref counts on
 12020                                  ;	open VCs. The VCs may be closed only at process termination.
 12021                                  ;
 12022                                  ;	If this is not an installed version of the DOS, file sharing will
 12023                                  ;	always be present.
 12024                                  ;
 12025                                  ;	We MUST always initialize lstclus to = firclus when regenerating a
 12026                                  ;	file. Otherwise we start allocating clusters up the wazoo.
 12027                                  ;
 12028                                  ;	Always initialize, during regeneration, the mode field to both isFCB
 12029                                  ;	and open_for_both. This is so the FCB code in the sharer can find the
 12030                                  ;	proper OI record.
 12031                                  ;
 12032                                  ;   The test bits are:
 12033                                  ;
 12034                                  ;	00 -> local file
 12035                                  ;	40 -> sharing local
 12036                                  ;	80 -> network
 12037                                  ;	C0 -> local device
 12038                                  
 12039                                  ;Break	<SaveFCBInfo - store pertinent information from an SFT into the FCB>
 12040                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 12041                                  ;
 12042                                  ;   SaveFCBInfo - given an FCB and its associated SFT, copy the relevant
 12043                                  ;	pieces of information into the FCB to allow for subsequent
 12044                                  ;	regeneration. Poke LRU also.
 12045                                  ;
 12046                                  ;   Inputs:	ThisSFT points to a complete SFT.
 12047                                  ;		DS:SI point to the FCB (not an extended one)
 12048                                  ;   Outputs:	The relevant reserved fields in the FCB are filled in.
 12049                                  ;		DS:SI preserved
 12050                                  ;		ES:DI point to sft
 12051                                  ;   Registers modified: All
 12052                                  ;
 12053                                  ;
 12054                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 12055                                  ;

 12259                                  ;Break	<ResetLRU - reset overflowed lru counts>
 12260                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 12261                                  ;
 12262                                  ;   ResetLRU - during lru updates, we may wrap at 64K. We must walk the
 12263                                  ;   entire set of SFTs and subtract 8000h from their lru counts and truncate
 12264                                  ;   at 0.
 12265                                  ;
 12266                                  ;   Inputs:	BX is offset into SFT field where lru firld is kept
 12267                                  ;		ES:DI point to SFT currently being updated
 12268                                  ;   Outputs:	All FCB SFTs have their lru fields truncated
 12269                                  ;		AX has 8000h
 12270                                  ;   Registers modified: none
 12271                                  ;
 12272                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 12273                                  ;
 12274                                  
 12275                                  	; 17/05/2019 - Retro DOS v4.0
 12276                                  ResetLRU:
 12277                                  	; ResetLRU is only called from fcbio.asm. So SS can be assumed to be 
 12278                                  	; DOSDATA

 12285                                  	;mov	cx,[es:di+4]

 12287                                  	;lea	di,[di+6]

 12575                                  ;
 12576                                  ; LruFCB -- allocate the LRU SFT from the SFT Table. The LRU scheme
 12577                                  ; maintains separate counts for net/Share and local SFTs. We allocate a 
 12578                                  ; net/Share SFT only if we do not find a local SFT. This helps keep
 12579                                  ; net/Share SFTs which cannot be regenerated for as long as possible. We
 12580                                  ; optimize regeneration operations by keeping track of the current local
 12581                                  ; SFT. This avoids scanning of the SFTs as long as we have at least one 
 12582                                  ; local SFT in the SFT Block.

 12585                                  ;	    = 1 => Allocate new SFT for Open/Create

 12589                                  ;	  	ThisSFT = Address of allocated SFT

 12593                                  ;

 13447                                  ;	the SFT for the FCB is Good. If so, make ThisSFT point to it. If not

 13573                                  ;Break <GetRR - return the random record field in DX:AX>
 13574                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 13575                                  ;
 13576                                  ;   GetRR - correctly load DX:AX with the random record field (3 or 4 bytes)
 13577                                  ;	from the FCB pointed to by DS:SI
 13578                                  ;
 13579                                  ;   Inputs:	DS:SI point to an FCB
 13580                                  ;		BX has record size
 13581                                  ;   Outputs:	DX:AX contain the contents of the random record field
 13582                                  ;   Registers modified: none

 13585                                  GetRR:

 13588                                  	;mov	dx,[si+23h]
 13589 00001BE5 8B5423                  	MOV	DX,[SI+SYS_FCB.RR+2]	; get high order part
 13590 00001BE8 83FB40                  	CMP	BX,64			; ignore MSB of RR if recsiz > 64

 13603                                  ;   Inputs:	DS:SI - point to FCB
 13604                                  ;   Outputs:	DX:AX contain the contents of the random record field

 13611                                  	;mov	dx,[si+0Ch]

 13613 00001BF6 D0E0                    	SHL	AL,1
 13614 00001BF8 D1EA                    	SHR	DX,1

 13624                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 13625                                  ;
 13626                                  ;   SetExtent - change the position of an FCB by filling in the extent/NR
 13627                                  ;	fields
 13628                                  ;
 13629                                  ;   Inputs:	DS:SI point to FCB
 13630                                  ;		DX:AX is a record location in file
 13631                                  ;   Outputs:	Extent/NR fields are filled in

 13640                                  	;mov	[si+20h],al
 13641 00001C08 884420                  	MOV	[SI+SYS_FCB.NR],AL
 13642 00001C0B 80E180                  	AND	CL,80H			; save upper bit
 13643 00001C0E D1E1                    	SHL	CX,1

 13645 00001C12 88E8                    	MOV	AL,CH

 13650 00001C1A 58                      	pop	ax

 13711                                  ;	and write a number of blocks from it.

 14361                                  
 14362                                  ; The SFT at ES:DI is the one that is already in use for this FCB. We set the
 14363                                  ; FCB to use this one. We increment its ref count. We do NOT close it at all.
 14364                                  ; Consider:
 14365                                  ;
 14366                                  ;   open (foo)	delete (foo) open (bar)
 14367                                  ;
 14368                                  ; This causes us to recycle (potentially) bar through the same local SFT as
 14369                                  ; foo even though foo is no longer needed; this is due to the server closing
 14370                                  ; foo for us when we delete it. Unfortunately, we cannot see this closure.
 14371                                  ; If we were to CLOSE bar, the server would then close the only reference to
 14372                                  ; bar and subsequent I/O would be lost to the redirector.
 14373                                  ;
 14374                                  ; This gets solved by NOT closing the sft, but zeroing the ref count
 14375                                  ; (effectively freeing the SFT) and informing the sharer (if relevant) that
 14376                                  ; the SFT is no longer in use. Note that the SHARER MUST keep its ref counts
 14377                                  ; around. This will allow us to access the same file through multiple network
 14378                                  ; connections and NOT prematurely terminate when the ref count on one
 14379                                  ; connection goes to zero.
 14380                                  
 14381                                  OpenFound:
 14382                                  	;mov	[si+18h],al
 14383 00001EA6 884418                  	MOV	[SI+fcb_sfn],AL 	; assign with this
 14384 00001EA9 26FF05                  	inc	word [es:di]
 14385                                  	;INC	word [ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_ref_count]
 14386                                  					; remember this new invocation
 14387                                  	; 24/01/2024
 14388 00001EAC 16                      	push	ss
 14389 00001EAD 1F                      	pop	ds
 14390                                  	
 14391                                  	;MOV	AX,[SS:FCBLRU]		; update LRU counts
 14392 00001EAE A1[1000]                	mov	ax,[FCBLRU] ; 24/01/2024
 14393                                  	;mov	[es:di+15h],ax
 14394 00001EB1 26894515                	MOV	[ES:DI+sf_LRU],AX
 14395                                  ;
 14396                                  ; We have an FCB sft that is now of no use. We release sharing info and then
 14397                                  ; blast it to prevent other reuse.
 14398                                  ;
 14399                                  	;push	ss
 14400                                  	;pop	ds
 14401                                  
 14402 00001EB5 C43E[9E05]              	LES	DI,[THISSFT]
 14403 00001EB9 26FF0D                  	dec	word [es:di]
 14404                                  	;DEC	word [ES:DI+SF_ENTRY.sf_ref_count]
 14405                                  					; free the newly allocated SFT

 14408 00001EC1 E845FC                  	call	BlastSFT

 14804                                  ;**	PackName - Convert file names from FCB to ASCIZ format.
 14805                                  ;
 14806                                  ;	PackName transfers a file name from DS:SI to ES:DI and converts it to
 14807                                  ;	the ASCIZ format.
 14808                                  ;
 14809                                  ;	ENTRY	(DS:SI) = 11 character FCB or dir entry name
 14810                                  ;		(ES:DI) = destination area (13 bytes)

 15136                                  ;BREAK <$ChDir -- Change current directory on a drive>
 15137                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 15138                                  ;
 15139                                  ; $ChDir - Top-level change directory system call.  This call is responsible
 15140                                  ; for setting up the CDS for the specified drive appropriately.  There are
 15141                                  ; several cases to consider:
 15142                                  ;
 15143                                  ;   o	Local, simple CDS.  In this case, we take the input path and convert
 15144                                  ;	it into a WFP.	We verify the existance of this directory and then
 15145                                  ;	copy the WFP into the CDS and set up the ID field to point to the
 15146                                  ;	directory cluster.
 15147                                  ;   o	Net CDS.  We form the path from the root (including network prefix)
 15148                                  ;	and verify its existance (via DOS_Chdir).  If successful, we copy the
 15149                                  ;	WFP back into the CDS.
 15150                                  ;   o	SUBST'ed CDS.  This is no different than the local, simple CDS.
 15151                                  ;   o	JOIN'ed CDS.  This is trouble as there are two CDS's at work.  If we
 15152                                  ;	call TransPath, we will get the PHYSICAL CDS that the path refers to
 15153                                  ;	and the PHYSICAL WFP that the input path refers to.  This is perfectly
 15154                                  ;	good for the validation but not for currency.  We call TransPathNoSet
 15155                                  ;	to process the path but to return the logical CDS and the logical
 15156                                  ;	path.  We then copy the logical path into the logical CDS.
 15157                                  ;
 15158                                  ; Inputs:
 15159                                  ;	DS:DX Points to asciz name
 15160                                  ; Returns:
 15161                                  ;	STD XENIX Return
 15162                                  ;	AX = chdir_path_not_found if error
 15163                                  ;
 15164                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 15165                                  
 15166                                  _$CHDIR:
 15167 00002128 BF[BE03]                	MOV	DI,OPENBUF		; spot for translated name
 15168 0000212B 89D6                    	MOV	SI,DX			; get source

 15170 00002130 7304                    	JNC	short ChDirCrack	; no errors, try path
 15171                                  ChDirErrP:
 15172                                  	;mov	al,3
 15173 00002132 B003                    	MOV	AL,error_path_not_found
 15174                                  ChDirErr:
 15175                                  	;jmp	SYS_RET_ERR 	; oops!
 15176                                  	; 10/11/2022 (MSDOS 5.0 MSDOS.SYS compatibility)
 15177 00002134 EBC9                    	jmp	short chdir_errj
 15178                                  
 15179                                  ChDirCrack:

 15181 0000213B 75F5                    	JNZ	short ChDirErrP

 15184                                  ; found.

 15191

 15199                                  ;

 15216                                  	;mov	ds,[si+0Eh]
 15217 0000215F 8E5C0E                  	MOV	DS,[SI+user_env.user_DS]
 15218

 15220 00002165 87F7                    	XCHG	SI,DI

 15383                                  ;**	IOCTL system call.
 15384                                  ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 15385                                  ;	$IOCTL
 15386                                  ;
 15387                                  ;	  Revision history:
 15388                                  ;
 15389                                  ;		Created: ARR 4 April 1983
 15390                                  ;
 15391                                  ;		GenericIOCTL added:		KGS	22 April 1985
 15392                                  ;
 15393                                  ;		A000	version 4.00	Jan. 1988
 15394                                  ;
 15395                                  ;		Used jump table to dispatch IOCTL functions. HKN 3/12/90
 15396                                  ;
 15397                                  
 15398                                  ;BREAK <IOCTL - munge on a handle to do device specific stuff>
 15399                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 15400                                  ;
 15401                                  ;   Assembler usage:
 15402                                  ;	    MOV     BX, Handle
 15403                                  ;	    MOV     DX, Data
 15404                                  ;
 15405                                  ;	(or LDS     DX,BUF
 15406                                  ;	    MOV     CX,COUNT)
 15407                                  ;
 15408                                  ;	    MOV     AH, Ioctl
 15409                                  ;	    MOV     AL, Request
 15410                                  ;	    INT     21h
 15411                                  ;
 15412                                  ;   AH = 0  Return a combination of low byte of sf_flags and device driver
 15413                                  ;	    attribute word in DX, handle in BX:
 15414                                  ;	    DH = high word of device driver attributes
 15415                                  ;	    DL = low byte of sf_flags
 15416                                  ;	 1  Set the bits contained in DX to sf_flags.  DH MUST be 0.  Handle
 15417                                  ;	    in BX.
 15418                                  ;	 2  Read CX bytes from the device control channel for handle in BX
 15419                                  ;	    into DS:DX.  Return number read in AX.
 15420                                  ;	 3  Write CX bytes to the device control channel for handle in BX from
 15421                                  ;	    DS:DX.  Return bytes written in AX.
 15422                                  ;	 4  Read CX bytes from the device control channel for drive in BX
 15423                                  ;	    into DS:DX.  Return number read in AX.
 15424                                  ;	 5  Write CX bytes to the device control channel for drive in BX from
 15425                                  ;	    DS:DX.  Return bytes written in AX.
 15426                                  ;	 6  Return input status of handle in BX. If a read will go to the
 15427                                  ;	    device, AL = 0FFh, otherwise 0.
 15428                                  ;	 7  Return output status of handle in BX. If a write will go to the
 15429                                  ;	    device, AL = 0FFh, otherwise 0.
 15430                                  ;	 8  Given a drive in BX, return 1 if the device contains non-
 15431                                  ;	    removable media, 0 otherwise.
 15432                                  ;	 9  Return the contents of the device attribute word in DX for the
 15433                                  ;	    drive in BX.  0200h is the bit for shared.	1000h is the bit for
 15434                                  ;	    network. 8000h is the bit for local use.
 15435                                  ;	 A  Return 8000h if the handle in BX is for the network or not.
 15436                                  ;	 B  Change the retry delay and the retry count for the system. BX is
 15437                                  ;	    the count and CX is the delay.
 15438                                  ;
 15439                                  ;   Error returns:
 15440                                  ;	    AX = error_invalid_handle
 15441                                  ;	       = error_invalid_function
 15442                                  ;	       = error_invalid_data
 15443                                  ;
 15444                                  ;-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 15445                                  ;
 15446                                  ;   This is the documentation copied from DOS 4.0 it is much better
 15447                                  ;   than the above
 15448                                  ;
 15449                                  ;	There are several basic forms of IOCTL calls:
 15450                                  ;
 15451                                  ;
 15452                                  ;	** Get/Set device information:	**
 15453                                  ;
 15454                                  ;	ENTRY	(AL) = function code
 15455                                  ;		  0 - Get device information
 15456                                  ;		  1 - Set device information
 15457                                  ;		(BX) = file handle
 15458                                  ;		(DX) = info for "Set Device Information"
 15459                                  ;	EXIT	'C' set if error
 15460                                  ;		  (AX) = error code
 15461                                  ;		'C' clear if OK
 15462                                  ;		  (DX) = info for "Get Device Information"
 15463                                  ;	USES	ALL
 15464                                  ;
 15465                                  ;
 15466                                  ;	**  Read/Write Control Data From/To Handle  **
 15467                                  ;
 15468                                  ;	ENTRY	(AL) = function code
 15469                                  ;		  2 - Read device control info
 15470                                  ;		  3 - Write device control info
 15471                                  ;		(BX) = file handle
 15472                                  ;		(CX) = transfer count
 15473                                  ;		(DS:DX) = address for data
 15474                                  ;	EXIT	'C' set if error
 15475                                  ;		  (AX) = error code
 15476                                  ;		'C' clear if OK
 15477                                  ;		  (AX) = count of bytes transfered
 15478                                  ;	USES	ALL
 15479                                  ;
 15480                                  ;
 15481                                  ;	**  Read/Write Control Data From/To Block Device  **
 15482                                  ;
 15483                                  ;	ENTRY	(AL) = function code
 15484                                  ;		  4 - Read device control info
 15485                                  ;		  5 - Write device control info
 15486                                  ;		(BL) = Drive number (0=default, 1='A', 2='B', etc)
 15487                                  ;		(CX) = transfer count
 15488                                  ;		(DS:DX) = address for data
 15489                                  ;	EXIT	'C' set if error
 15490                                  ;		  (AX) = error code
 15491                                  ;		'C' clear if OK
 15492                                  ;		  (AX) = count of bytes transfered
 15493                                  ;	USES	ALL
 15494                                  ;
 15495                                  ;
 15496                                  ;	**  Get Input/Output Status  **
 15497                                  ;
 15498                                  ;	ENTRY	(AL) = function code
 15499                                  ;		  6 - Get Input status
 15500                                  ;		  7 - Get Output Status
 15501                                  ;		(BX) = file handle
 15502                                  ;	EXIT	'C' set if error
 15503                                  ;		  (AX) = error code
 15504                                  ;		'C' clear if OK
 15505                                  ;		  (AL) = 00 if not ready
 15506                                  ;		  (AL) = FF if ready
 15507                                  ;	USES	ALL
 15508                                  ;
 15509                                  ;
 15510                                  ;	**  Get Drive Information  **
 15511                                  ;
 15512                                  ;	ENTRY	(AL) = function code
 15513                                  ;		  8 - Check for removable media
 15514                                  ;		  9 - Get device attributes
 15515                                  ;		(BL) = Drive number (0=default, 1='A', 2='B', etc)
 15516                                  ;	EXIT	'C' set if error
 15517                                  ;		  (AX) = error code
 15518                                  ;		'C' clear if OK
 15519                                  ;		  (AX) = 0/1 media is removable/fixed (func. 8)
 15520                                  ;		  (DX) = device attribute word (func. 9)
 15521                                  ;	USES	ALL
 15522                                  ;
 15523                                  ;
 15524                                  ;	**  Get Redirected bit	**
 15525                                  ;
 15526                                  ;	ENTRY	(AL) = function code
 15527                                  ;		  0Ah - Network stuff
 15528                                  ;		(BX) = file handle
 15529                                  ;	EXIT	'C' set if error
 15530                                  ;		  (AX) = error code
 15531                                  ;		'C' clear if OK
 15532                                  ;		  (DX) = SFT flags word, 8000h set if network file
 15533                                  ;	USES	ALL
 15534                                  ;
 15535                                  ;
 15536                                  ;	**  Change sharer retry parameters  **
 15537                                  ;
 15538                                  ;	ENTRY	(AL) = function code
 15539                                  ;		  0Bh - Set retry parameters
 15540                                  ;		(CX) = retry loop count
 15541                                  ;		(DX) = number of retries
 15542                                  ;	EXIT	'C' set if error
 15543                                  ;		  (AX) = error code
 15544                                  ;		'C' clear if OK
 15545                                  ;	USES	ALL
 15546                                  ;
 15547                                  ;
 15548                                  ;   =================================================================
 15549                                  ;
 15550                                  ;	**  New Standard Control  **
 15551                                  ;
 15552                                  ;	ALL NEW IOCTL FACILITIES SHOULD USE THIS FORM.	THE OTHER
 15553                                  ;	FORMS ARE OBSOLETE.
 15554                                  ;
 15555                                  ;   =================================================================
 15556                                  ;
 15557                                  ;	ENTRY	(AL) = function code
 15558                                  ;		  0Ch - Control Function subcode
 15559                                  ;		(BX) = File Handle
 15560                                  ;		(CH) = Category Indicator
 15561                                  ;		(CL) = Function within category
 15562                                  ;		(DS:DX) = address for data, if any
 15563                                  ;		(SI) = Passed to device as argument, use depends upon function
 15564                                  ;		(DI) = Passed to device as argument, use depends upon function
 15565                                  ;	EXIT	'C' set if error
 15566                                  ;		  (AX) = error code
 15567                                  ;		'C' clear if OK
 15568                                  ;		  (SI) = Return value, meaning is function dependent
 15569                                  ;		  (DI) = Return value, meaning is function dependent
 15570                                  ;		  (DS:DX) = Return address, use is function dependent
 15571                                  ;	USES	ALL
 15572                                  ;
 15573                                  ;    ============== Generic IOCTL Definitions for DOS 3.2 ============
 15574                                  ;     (See inc\ioctl.inc for more info)
 15575                                  ;
 15576                                  ;	ENTRY	(AL) = function code
 15577                                  ;		  0Dh - Control Function subcode
 15578                                  ;		(BL) = Drive Number (0 = Default, 1= 'A')
 15579                                  ;		(CH) = Category Indicator
 15580                                  ;		(CL) = Function within category
 15581                                  ;		(DS:DX) = address for data, if any
 15582                                  ;		(SI) = Passed to device as argument, use depends upon function
 15583                                  ;		(DI) = Passed to device as argument, use depends upon function
 15584                                  ;
 15585                                  ;	EXIT	'C' set if error
 15586                                  ;		  (AX) = error code
 15587                                  ;		'C' clear if OK
 15588                                  ;		  (DS:DX) = Return address, use is function dependent
 15589                                  ;	USES	ALL
 15590                                  ;
 15591                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 15592

 15796                                  ;
 15797                                  ; Generic IOCTL entry point. AL = C, D, 10h, 11h
 15798                                  ;
 15799                                  ;	here we invoke the Generic IOCTL using the IOCTL_Req structure.
 15800                                  ;	SI:DX -> Users Device Parameter Table
 15801                                  ;	IOCALL -> IOCTL_Req structure
 15802                                  ;
 15803                                  ; 	If on entry AL >= IOCTL_QUERY_HANDLE the function is a
 15804                                  ;	QueryIOCtlSupport call ELSE it's a standard generic IOCtl
 15805                                  ;	call.
 15806                                  ;
 15807                                  ; BUGBUG: Don't push anything on the stack between GENERIOCTL: and 
 15808                                  ;         the call to Check_If_Net because Check_If_Net gets our
 15809                                  ;         return address off the stack if the drive is invalid.
 15810                                  ;
 15811                                  ;--------------------------------------------------------------------------
