 46970                                  
 46971                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 46972                                  ;
 46973                                  ; LowIntXX:
 46974                                  ;
 46975                                  ; Interrupts from DOS that pass control to a user program must be done from
 46976                                  ; low memory, as the user program may change the state of the A20 line or
 46977                                  ; they may require that the A20 line be OFF. The following piece of code is
 46978                                  ; far call'd from the following places in DOS:
 46979                                  ;
 46980                                  ;	1. msctrlc.asm where dos issues an int 23h (ctrlc)
 46981                                  ;	2. msctrlc.asm where dos issues an int 24h (critical error)
 46982                                  ;	3. msctrlc.asm where dos issues an int 28h (idle int)
 46983                                  ;
 46984                                  ; The int 23 and int 24 handlers may decide to do a far return instead of an
 46985                                  ; IRET ane leave the flags on the stack. Therefore we save the return address
 46986                                  ; before doing the ints and then do a far junp back into DOS.
 46987                                  ;
 46988                                  ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 46989                                  
 46990 000010DB 00000000                DosRetAddr23:	dd	0
 46991 000010DF 00000000                DosRetAddr24:	dd	0
 46992 000010E3 00000000                DosRetAddr28:	dd	0
 46993                                  
 46994                                  	; Execute int 23h from low memory
 46995                                  LowInt23:
 46996                                  					; save the return address that is on
 46997                                  					; the stack
 46998 000010E7 2E8F06[DB10]            	pop	word [cs:DosRetAddr23]
 46999 000010EC 2E8F06[DD10]            	pop	word [cs:DosRetAddr23+2]
 47000                                  
 47001 000010F1 CD23                    	int	23h			; ctrl C
 47002                                  					; turn on A20 it has been turned OFF
 47003                                  					; by int 28/23/24 handler.
 47004                                  
 47005 000010F3 E87900                  	call	EnsureA20ON		; M011: we must turn on A20 if OFF
 47006                                  
 47007 000010F6 2EFF2E[DB10]            	jmp	far [cs:DosRetAddr23]	; jump back to DOS
 47008                                  
 47009                                  
 47010                                  	; Execute int 24h from low memory
 47011                                  LowInt24:
 47012                                  					; save the return address that is on
 47013                                  					; the stack
 47014 000010FB 2E8F06[DF10]            	pop	word [cs:DosRetAddr24]
 47015 00001100 2E8F06[E110]            	pop	word [cs:DosRetAddr24+2]
 47016                                  
 47017 00001105 CD24                    	int	24h			; crit error
 47018                                  					; turn on A20 it has been turned OFF
 47019                                  					; by int 28/23/24 handler.
 47020                                  
 47021 00001107 E86500                  	call	EnsureA20ON		; M011: we must turn on A20 if OFF
 47022                                  
 47023 0000110A 2EFF2E[DF10]            	jmp	far [cs:DosRetAddr24]	; jump back to DOS
 47024                                  
 47025                                  
 47026                                  	; Execute int 28h from low memory
 47027                                  LowInt28:
 47028 0000110F CD28                    	int	28h			; idle int
 47029                                  					; turn on A20 it has been turned OFF
 47030                                  					; by int 28/23/24 handler.
 47031                                  
 47032 00001111 E85B00                  	call	EnsureA20ON		; M011: we must turn on A20 if OFF
 47033                                  
 47034 00001114 CB                      	retf
 47035                                  
 47036                                  ; DOSDATA:1115h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
 47037                                  
 47038                                  ;-------------------------------------------------------------------------
 47039                                  ;
 47040                                  ; int 21 ah=4b (exec) call will jump to the following label before xferring
 47041                                  ; control to the exec'd program. We turn off A20 inorder to allow programs
 47042                                  ; that have been packed by the faulty exepack utility to unpack correctly.
 47043                                  ; This is so because exepac'd programs rely on address wrap.
 47044                                  ;
 47045                                  ;-------------------------------------------------------------------------
 47046                                  
 47047                                  disa20_xfer:
 47048 00001115 E83F00                  	call	XMMDisableA20		; disable A20
 47049                                  
 47050                                  	; Look at msproc.asm at label exec_go for understanding the following:
 47051                                  
 47052                                  	; DS:SI points to entry point
 47053                                  	; AX:DI points to initial stack
 47054                                  	; DX has PDB pointer
 47055                                  	; BX has initial AX value
 47056                                  
 47057 00001118 FA                      	cli
 47058 00001119 2EC606[2103]00          	mov	byte [cs:INDOS],0	; SS Override
 47059                                  
 47060 0000111F 8ED0                    	mov	SS,AX			; set up user's stack
 47061 00001121 89FC                    	mov	SP,DI			; and SP
 47062 00001123 FB                      	sti
 47063                                  
 47064 00001124 1E                      	push	DS			; fake long call to entry
 47065 00001125 56                      	push	SI
 47066 00001126 8EC2                    	mov	ES,DX			; set up proper seg registers
 47067 00001128 8EDA                    	mov	DS,DX
 47068 0000112A 89D8                    	mov	AX,BX			; set up proper AX
 47069 0000112C CB                      	retf
 47070                                  
 47071                                  ;-------------------------------------------------------------------------
 47072                                  ;
 47073                                  ; M003:
 47074                                  ;
 47075                                  ; If an int 21 ah=25 call is made immediately after an exec call, DOS will
 47076                                  ; come here, turn A20 OFF restore user stack and registers before returning
 47077                                  ; to user. This is done in dos\msdisp.asm. This has been done to support
 47078                                  ; programs compiled with MS PASCAL 3.2. See under TAG M003 in DOSSYM.INC for
 47079                                  ; more info.
 47080                                  ;
 47081                                  ; Also at this point DS is DOSDATA. So we can assume DS DOSDATA. Note that
 47082                                  ; SS is also DOS stack. It is important that we do the XMS call on DOS's
 47083                                  ; stack to avoid additional stack overhead for the user.
 47084                                  ;
 47085                                  ; -------------------------------------------------------------------------
 47086                                  
 47087                                  disa20_iret:
 47088 0000112D E82700                  	call	XMMDisableA20
 47089 00001130 FE0E[2103]              	dec	byte [INDOS]
 47090 00001134 8E16[8605]              	mov	SS,[USER_SS]		; restore user stack
 47091 00001138 8B26[8405]              	mov	SP,[USER_SP]
 47092 0000113C 89E5                    	mov	BP,SP
 47093                                  	;mov	[BP+user_env.user_AX],AL
 47094 0000113E 884600                  	mov	[bp],al
 47095 00001141 A1[F205]                	mov	AX,[NSP]
 47096 00001144 A3[8405]                	mov	[USER_SP],AX
 47097 00001147 A1[F005]                	mov	AX,[NSS]
 47098 0000114A A3[8605]                	mov	[USER_SS],AX
 47099                                  
 47100 0000114D 58                      	pop	AX			; restore user regs
 47101 0000114E 5B                      	pop	BX
 47102 0000114F 59                      	pop	CX
 47103 00001150 5A                      	pop	DX
 47104 00001151 5E                      	pop	SI
 47105 00001152 5F                      	pop	DI
 47106 00001153 5D                      	pop	BP
 47107 00001154 1F                      	pop	DS
 47108 00001155 07                      	pop	ES
 47109 00001156 CF                      	iret
 47110

 47112                                  ;***	XMMDisableA20 - switch 20th address line
 47113                                  ;
 47114                                  ;	This routine is used to disable the 20th address line in
 47115                                  ;	the system using XMM calls.
 47116                                  ;
 47117                                  ;	ENTRY	none		;ds = _DATA
 47118                                  ;	EXIT	A20 line disabled
 47119                                  ;	USES	NOTHING
 47120                                  ;

 47177 00001175 2EC536[6711]            	lds	si,[cs:LowMemory]	; Compare the 4 words at 0000:0080
 47178 0000117A 2EC43E[6B11]            	les	di,[cs:HighMemory]	; with the 4 at FFFF:0090
 47179                                  
 47180                                  	; 25/03/2024
 47181                                  	;xor	di,di

 47690                                  ;============================================================================
 47691                                  ; MPATCH.ASM (MSDOS 6.0, 1993)
 47692                                  ;============================================================================
 47693                                  ; 27/04/2019 - Retro DOS 4.0
 47694                                  
 47695                                  ;mpatch.asm -- holds data patch location for callouts 
 47696                                  ; -- allocate cluster in rom.asm
 47697                                  ;
 47698                                  ; This area is pointed to by OffsetMagicPatch[609h] in fixed DOS data.
 47699                                  ; Currently, this location is used only by magicdrv.sys's patch to
 47700                                  ; cluster allocation, however it can be expanded to be used by other
 47701                                  ; patches. This is important since we have an easy-access pointer to
 47702                                  ; this location in OffsetMagicPatch. Magicdrv.sys is guaranteed to
 47703                                  ; only patch out a far call/retf, so any space after that could be
 47704                                  ; used as a patch by using OffsetMagicPatch+6. See rom.asm on how
 47705                                  ; to call out here.
 47706                                  ;
 47707                                  ; Currently, we allocate only the minimum space required for the 6
 47708                                  ; byte magicdrv patch, so if you change the dos data, you may want
 47709                                  ; to reserve space here if your new data will be position dependent
 47710                                  ; and would prohibit growing of this table.
 47711                                  ;
 47712                                  ;history	-	created 8-7-92 by scottq
 47713                                  ;		-	added Rational386PatchPtr 2-1-93 by jimmat
 47714                                  ;
 47715                                  ;Exported Functions
 47716                                  ;==================
 47717                                  ;MagicPatch     -       callout patched by magidrv.sys for cluster allocations
 47718                                  
 47719                                  ; DosData Segment
 47720                                  
 47721                                  ; DOSDATA:1362h (MSDOS 6.21, MSDOS.SYS)
 47722                                  
 47723                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 47724                                  
 47725                                  ; Rational386PatchPtr points to either a RET instruction (80286 or less) or
 47726                                  ; a routine to fix buggy versions of the Rational DOS Extender (80386 or
 47727                                  ; greater). Added to this file because it needed to be somewhere and is
 47728                                  ; 'patch' related.
 47729                                  
 47730                                  Rational386PatchPtr:
 47731                                  	dw	0	; points to patch routine or RET instr.
 47732                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 47733                                  
 47734                                  MagicPatch:
 47735                                  ;MagicPatch proc far
 47736                                          retf            ;default is to just return to allocate
 47737                                          nop             ;however, this code will be patched
 47738                                          nop             ;by magicdrv.sys to
 47739                                          nop             ; call far ?:?     
 47740                                          nop             ; retf or perhaps just jmp far
 47741                                          nop             ;retf/nop take one byte, so we need six instructions
 47742                                                          ;for 6 byte patch
 47743                                  ;MagicPatch endp
 47744                                  
 47745                                  ; ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 47746                                  
 47747                                  ;DosData Ends
 47748                                  
 47749                                  ; DOSDATA:136Ah
 47750
